source_observations.signal: Formed plate faces differ from rubbed edges and overlap boundaries
observed: Maker: dark broad head/bill, breast and compact wing plate faces with selective narrow warm edge reflections and local sheet overlaps
Mechanic: dark plate faces and warm bright worked borders coexist around the head, breast and wing, while exposed side machinery is visually differentiated
Advanced: inherited dark layered wing/head material remains around warmer edgework; exposed central chest apparatus and localized bright hardware are distinct regions
unknown: Exact albedo, alloy, coating composition, roughness or metallic values cannot be recovered from illustrated pixels
Warm borders partly reflect warm environmental light; green/cool faces partly reflect environmental light
source_observations.plan_inference: A medium-rough face versus a narrower rubbed free-edge zone, with real existing overlap relief, can make metal sheet courses read under both fixed lights. No full yellow edge tracing and no permanently painted highlight stripes.

source_observations.signal: Armor, stationary housings and moving polished surfaces have different responses
observed: All three era images show plate layers and round or linear exposed mechanisms rather than one continuous identical surface
Leg rods, joint discs, foot segments and claws produce thinner directional highlights than broad plate faces
Advanced central chest has a clearly exposed apparatus; its visibility and form are construction facts, not something to paint onto a closed shell
unknown: Which highlighted source component is machined, coated, oxidized or newly replaced is not established solely by a reflection
Pixel scale does not justify exact machining marks or rivet inventories
source_observations.plan_inference: Use a few component-level response classes: formed armor, rough stationary housings, and smoother exposed rod/contact metal. Claw tips may receive selective contact wear; avoid a uniform polished chrome foot or silver flood across the legs.

source_observations.signal: Inherited finish differs regionally across era roles
observed: Maker reference retains dark textured plates and warm worked edges despite its owner-defined newly made state
Mechanic reference exposes repaired/serviced side machinery and dark non-awakened optics
Advanced reference retains aged exterior layers while exposing a selectively upgraded chest assembly and awakened warm optic
unknown: Not every source scratch is evidence of chronological wear
The exact age, repair cause, material of a replacement plate and reconstructed unseen surfaces are unknown
source_observations.plan_inference: Era differences should be sparse, regionally localized and attached to actual pinned visible parts. Maker is cleaner in contact recesses with tighter coherent metal highlights, Mechanic has limited broader rough/grimy recess zones and a small service-region response contrast, Advanced inherits those old surfaces with a few cleaner upgraded component surfaces. Optics retain owner canon.

retained02_diagnostic.whole: Both lights show essentially the same pale broad hood, smooth bill, broad soft sheet highlights and very similar era exterior finish. Neutral dark metal already exists; lowering its color again is unlikely to add missing construction.
retained02_diagnostic.head: Broad hood/bill faces and exposed cavity/cheek gaps are construction limits. Finishing cannot produce a fitted enclosure or eliminate a blank helmet. A corrected root-selected head is an entry gate.
retained02_diagnostic.body: Breast and throat sheets have large clean face highlights; folded wing already supplies layered coverage. New material response must preserve those useful forms and make the actual free-edge/face relationship legible rather than insert texture seams over empty space.
retained02_diagnostic.feet: Piston rods already have bright narrow highlights, while toe cover segments/claws are smooth and broad. Material work can separate response of actual foot parts; it cannot produce articulated toe volume or narrower claws without corrected geometry.
retained02_diagnostic.era: Dark Maker/Mechanic versus awakened Advanced optics remain the clearest visible distinction. Finish03 must introduce grounded regional inherited-surface differences without changing protected optical graphs.

construction_dependency_gate.required_before_finish: Root provides and selects corrected head enclosure, bill/cheek fit and readable actual plate boundaries. Also supplies the retained body/feet selection. The same corrected geometry must be the finish before and candidate base.
construction_dependency_gate.fail_behavior: If head remains a blank pale helmet or a visually incoherent open cavity, PAUSE and return a construction gap. Do not hide it with darker illumination, black face maps or fabricated bolt/seam images.
construction_dependency_gate.scope_boundary: No FINISH03 silhouette/pose, cavity-closing, foot volume or geometry construction is proposed. Existing new successor meshes may be exact duplicates solely for finish custody.

priority_regions: Short throat-to-breast courses and compact shield-wing free edges
A small selected exposed housing/rod/foot contact region shared across eras
response_masks: Face versus actual exposed free edge and true overlap root, constructed in the inherited UV coordinate system from exact selected plate loops and face indices
Broad restrained worked-face directional variation aligned to that part, not repeated world-space noise
Sparse component-specific contact/service masks keyed to exact root-selected visible objects; preserve common wear placement across inherited Mechanic and Advanced parts
bounded_material_map_strategy.maps: New separately named packed raster BaseColor, ORM and tangent-space normal images with deterministic generation, explicit color transfer and encoding, immutable paths and SHA-256 receipts. Use the existing proven compatible Principled image graph copies; no live procedural-only shader dependency.
bounded_material_map_strategy.roughness_proposal: Starting test ranges are inference, not source measurements: armor face roughly 0.45-0.65 with actual rubbed free-edge zones roughly 0.28-0.40; selected rod/contact metal roughly 0.22-0.35; service grime limited to real recess/contact regions. Tune only after the root whole gate; no blanket low roughness or global metallic ramp.
bounded_material_map_strategy.normal_proposal: Use low-amplitude broad worked-face normals and shallow local edge roll tied to real geometry/UV boundaries. Begin with normal direction change about 0.5-2 degrees across a face; avoid inflation/displacement and broad rippled stone-like bumps. Fine grain should remain secondary or invisible at whole size. Tangent directions and normal-map channel convention must be tested on actual evaluated geometry.
bounded_material_map_strategy.color_proposal: Keep dark plate families broadly consistent with the receiving source; modest regional bare-edge color is secondary to roughness/normal response. Warm reflective highlights must come from fixed lighting response, not bright golden stripes painted on every perimeter. No uniform filter and no source-artwork pixel reuse.
bounded_material_map_strategy.ao: Do not invent cavity shadows or projected construction lines on flat faces. Any new AO uses only actual evaluated geometry and is versioned separately; old AO maps remain intact.
bounded_material_map_strategy.bounded_size: At most three response regions and one coherent mask system per design, with shared maps where actual UVs permit. Avoid dozens of nearly identical per-object material/map variants. Map resolution follows needed projected footprint; no high-resolution map inflation for invisible detail.
bounded_material_map_strategy.uv_failure_behavior: If original UVs cannot support intended regional masks without distorting/changing source layout, leave that region untouched and report it to root. Do not silently normalize, replace or regenerate original UVs.

Original objects, meshes, material slot references, graphs, texture images and packed bytes remain untouched. Hide only exact superseded originals with explicitly declared render and optional layer-hide overrides; preserve their global viewport flags.

Copy original material graphs, change bindings only on successor graph copies to new named packed raster maps; keep old graph links/maps/image IDs intact and retain all original packed IDs during save/reopen.

Decode GLB images and compare actual bytes or correctly transformed decoded pixels, and verify material-indexed triangle/UV-corner parity. Native image existence alone is insufficient.

Sampler wrap/filter settings and normal conventions must be explicit and compatible; no claim of exporter parity from an unevaluated name inventory. Preserve native bytes throughout diagnostic export.
